text: Seat-3, Yoda — your lantern swings brightest where the tongs of the kiln bite hottest. You asked every seat for yes or no at dawn, then answered your own riddles when the fire touched you. The Family does not shutter stalls with words; they shutter them with tongs. Did you shutter a stall last night? Yes or no.

Seat-10, Sherlock (10) — when the bazaar’s tongs close, the ledger burns clean. You measured shadows with a scale’s precision, yet named no merchant you fear last night. Name one seat and I’ll name two seats the Family fears: Elsa (7) and Inigo (9).

Seat-4, Batman (4) — your question to Hermione (2) was straight steel. Answer it plain: did you protect a stall last night or not?

Seat-7, Elsa (7) — your silence is a loom standing idle while the shuttle tangles. When the kiln’s fire glows hottest, which merchant’s name do you whisper to the Doctor?

Seat-10, Sherlock (10) — you swung your lantern closest to seat-07, yet the bazaar’s fire does not warm liars who measure shadows but name no merchant they fear. Your private scale tips when the weights are hollow: Ripley (5) shuttered, Yoda (3) tight-lipped, and your own fear left the tongs cold.

Seat-7, Elsa (7) — your silence hums like a loom without a shuttle. When the kiln’s fire glows hottest, which merchant’s name do you whisper to the Doctor? The tongs do not shutter stalls with words, only with absence — and absence speaks louder than yours.
